beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "We landed a bigger contract. My partner wants to start Monday. I want two more weeks to plan it properly."

options.text: Sounds like you're both pulling toward the same finish, just at different speeds.
Then you two clearly shouldn't be in business together.
Whoever's more senior should just decide.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Maybe. It just feels like we're fighting each other instead of the actual deadline."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: Two forces pulling the same cart — the trick is aligning them, not picking one.
One of you has to give up control entirely.
This card means the deal is doomed either way.

elaboration: The Chariot isn't pulled by one horse — it's pulled by two, and the whole card is about getting them moving the same direction instead of against each other.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "But my gut says start now, and his spreadsheet says wait. Which one's actually right?"

options.text: Neither wins alone — it's the two together that actually move you.
The spreadsheet is always right over a gut feeling.
Gut feelings don't belong in business decisions.

elaboration: The Chariot only moves when instinct and reason pull together — treating the emotional read as fuel instead of a distraction is the actual win.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Okay. Let's find a start date that both horses can live with."
